items.description: All images have meaningful alt text (not just filenames)
Decorative images use empty alt (alt="") or CSS background
Complex images (charts, graphs) have long descriptions or data tables
Icon fonts have text alternatives (aria-label or hidden text)
Pre-recorded audio-only content has transcript
Pre-recorded video has captions
Pre-recorded video has audio description or alternative
Live video has captions (AA requirement)
Information and relationships conveyed through presentation are available in text
Heading hierarchy is logical (h1 → h2 → h3, no skips)
Lists are marked up as <ul> or <ol>, not just visual bullets
Data tables use <th> with scope or <caption>
Content reading order matches visual order
Instructions don't rely solely on shape, size, or location
Content is not locked to portrait or landscape only (AA 2.1)
Input fields collect common purposes (name, email) with autocomplete (AA 2.1)
User interface components have accessible names matching their purpose (AAA)
Color is not the only way to convey information (links underlined, error icons)
Auto-playing audio has a pause/stop mechanism within 3 seconds
Text contrast meets 4.5:1 (3:1 large text) — automated check complements
Text resizes up to 200% without loss of content or functionality
Text is used instead of images of text (except logos)
Content reflows without scroll at 320px wide (AA 2.1)
UI components and graphical objects have 3:1 contrast (AA 2.1)
No content or functionality loss with custom text spacing (AA 2.1)
Hover/focus-triggered content is dismissible, hoverable, and persistent (AA 2.1)
All functionality is operable through keyboard interface
No keyboard focus is trapped in a component (escape to dismiss)
No single-key shortcuts unless remappable or disabled by default (AA 2.1)
Time limits have options to turn off, adjust, or extend
Moving, blinking, auto-updating content has pause/stop/hide controls
Non-essential interruptions (alerts, updates) can be postponed or suppressed (AAA)
No content flashes more than 3 times per second
No content flashes more than 3 times in any 1-second period (AA)
Skip-to-content link is present and functional
Pages have descriptive <title> that identifies purpose
Focus order follows a logical sequence matching visual order
Link purpose is clear from link text alone or with context
Multiple ways to find a page (nav, sitemap, search) (AA)
Headings and labels describe topic or purpose (AA)
Keyboard focus indicator is visible (AA)
Focus indicator is not fully hidden by author-created content (AA 2.2)
Focus indicator area is at least 2 CSS px thick with 3:1 contrast (AA 2.2)
Functionality using multipoint gestures can also be operated via single point (AA 2.1)
Down-event is not used unless up-event cancels or is essential (AA 2.1)
Visible label matches accessible name (AA 2.1)
Dragging alternatives exist for all drag movements (AA 2.2)
Click targets are at least 24x24 CSS px (AA 2.2)
Page has a language attribute on the <html> element
Language changes in content are marked with lang attribute (AA)
Text requires reading ability no higher than lower secondary education (AAA)
Pronunciation guidance for ambiguous words (AAA)
No context change when component receives focus
No unexpected context change on input (AA)
Navigation appears in the same order on each page (AA)
Components with same functionality are identified consistently (AA)
Help mechanisms appear in consistent location (AA 2.2)
Errors are identified and described in text
Labels or instructions are provided for all inputs
Error suggestions are provided when known (AA)
Legal, financial, or form submissions are reversible or confirmed (AA)
Previously entered info is auto-populated or selectable (AA 2.2)
Authentication does not rely on cognitive function tests (AA 2.2)
No major HTML parsing errors (duplicate IDs, unclosed tags)
Custom widgets have appropriate name, role, and value in accessibility API
Status messages are announced via role="status" or aria-live (AA 2.1)
